summary: State-built 1927 lookout in Moultonborough, NH; closed by the state in 1981; now operated by a private association on Lakes Region Conservation Trust land; height sources disagree.

facts.design: 27-foot steel tower with a 10-by-10 wooden cab, erected in 1927

access.note: A sign marks the trailhead, on Lakes Region Conservation Trust land. The sources do not say whether the stairs or cab are open to visitors now. A 2016 visit report found rotting landings.

visit.trail_note: A sign before the trailhead marks the tower, per the 2016 visit report.

facts.agency: Lakes Region Conservation Trust (landowner); tower operated by a private association

events.note: Built by the State of New Hampshire as a replacement for the Mt. Israel lookout. Eastern lookouts says the 27-foot tower was erected with $1175 in private funds and then given to the state.
Height change disputed. The register says the tower was raised to 55 feet and given an observation platform. Eastern lookouts says a 10-foot extension brought it to 37 feet.
Closed by the state. The Town of Moultonborough then signed a lease, and the local fire department took over detection duties.
Town received a Forest Fire Lookout Association restoration grant to repaint the tower. No painting followed.

Inspections in June and November found no work done and no attempt to paint the cab or steelwork. In December the selectmen voted to end the town's lease and return the site to the Lakes Region Conservation Trust.
The effort to operate the tower did not succeed, and the grant money was sent to the FFLA treasurer to close the matter.
Visit report: needs paint; wood on every landing rotting and not properly secured. The visitor found the tower apparently staffed by Moultonborough residents but not staffed that day.
Continues to be operated by a private association

corrections.proposed: 16.8 (55 ft per the register; disputed, Eastern lookouts gives 37 ft / 11.3 m)
corrections.why: 8.2 m is the original 27-foot height from 1927, not the current height. The register says a 1972 extension raised the tower to 55 feet, but Eastern lookouts says 37 feet. The sources disagree, so the editor should choose; height_m was left out of the facts.
The 2011 chapter report says the Town received the FFLA restoration grant in 2009.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the 1972 work raised the tower to 55 feet. Eastern lookouts says a 10-foot extension brought it to 37 feet. The story reports both and does not choose.

A 2016 visitor saw the tower apparently staffed by Moultonborough residents, though it was not staffed that day. The 2025 chapter report says a private association operates it. The story uses the 2025 report as the current account.

notes_for_editor: The NHLR page read for this brief has no 2010 shingle-replacement entry and no 2010 grant entry, so the brief's 2010 'restored' event could not be confirmed. The 2011 report gives 2009 for the grant, which is the basis of the correction. The 1972 height is disputed (55 ft register vs 37 ft Eastern lookouts) and height_m was left out of the facts. Current access terms for the stairs and cab were not found, so access.level is unknown and the story does not encourage climbing given the 2016 landing report. The 2025 report does not say who the private association is. The Town of Moultonborough flyer, the Red Hill Tower Watchman Facebook page and the trail-site snippets were not opened.
